title: Consensus of scholars
hookLine: agreement of the scholars as a source for Sunni schools

cards: What happens when the people who know a subject best all land in the same place? In Sunni legal thought, that landing place has a name, and it counts as a source of law in its own right, after the Qur'an and the sunnah.
Not a vote. Not a poll of the public. The agreement of the community's qualified scholars on a ruling.
It sounds simple. Pinning down what it means, whose agreement counts, and how anyone could know it happened, kept scholars arguing. Today: ijma'.

teach.b: Ijma' means agreement, a coming together on one thing. In Sunni legal theory it names the agreement of the qualified scholars of the community, in a given generation, on a ruling. The grounds?

Scholars point to a report that the Prophet ﷺ said his community would not agree upon error. It comes in more than one collection, in different wordings, and critics have weighed its chains differently.
Tradition says al-Shafi'i also pointed to a verse that warns against following a way other than the believers' way. What does consensus do? Where it exists, it settles a question.
Scholars give examples like the obligation of the daily prayers and the fast of Ramadan, or the gathering of the Qur'an into one written copy that was passed on.
And they hold that consensus rests on a text; it doesn't float free of the Qur'an and the sunnah. Then the arguments about agreement itself.
Whose agreement counts? Only the companions'? The scholars of any generation?
Imam Malik gave special weight to the practice of the people of Medina. Can a consensus even be known, once scholars live scattered across many lands?
A saying attributed to Ahmad ibn Hanbal warns that someone who claims consensus may be speaking falsely, since people may have differed without his knowing.
And Twelver Shia scholars accept consensus as proof when it reveals the view of the Imam, not as a source standing on its own.
So agreement is itself a place where scholars disagree, carefully, which shows how much weight they gave it.

how: Sunni scholars treat a ruling on which the qualified scholars agreed as settled, while Twelver Shia scholars accept consensus when it reflects the view of the Imam; students learn which rulings are held to be agreed and which are differed over.

o: a vote of all Muslims on a new question of law
the agreement of qualified scholars on a ruling
the ruling of a single great scholar of an age

p: a report scholars cite for consensus
consensus that reveals the Imam's view

s: ijma' means a popular vote of all Muslims
it is the agreement of the qualified scholars on a ruling, not a poll of the public.
Twelver Shia scholars accept consensus when it reveals the view of the Imam
for them it is proof through the Imam, not a source standing alone.
scholars all agree on how consensus works
whose agreement counts, and whether it can be known, are argued over.

games.q: you're a scholar asked about a question, and you find that the scholars before you agreed on the answer. what do you do?
o: set their agreement aside and start from scratch.
treat the agreement as settling it, and look for the text it rests on.
put the question to a public vote.
games.why: in Sunni legal theory, a real consensus settles the question, and it is expected to rest on a text. the hard part, scholars said, is knowing the agreement was real.

practice: Take one ruling scholars give as an example of consensus: the fast of Ramadan is obligatory. Picture its reach, people of different schools, lands and languages, who differ on a great deal, all keeping the same month.
Hold that picture for a few breaths.

wordCard.voice: Ijma'. Agreement: in Sunni law, the agreement of the community's qualified scholars on a ruling, a source standing after the Qur'an and the sunnah. Today's word.
